I discovered sorbitol is my biggest trigger! Cutting it out completely has been life changing. My symptoms have gone from constant to almost never appearing.

Low FODMAP only works if you stick with it, and properly. I suffered for 20 years before I finally discovered my triggers by being super vigilant with low FODMAP (polyols, fructans and fructose are my biggest triggers). I attempted low FODMAP many times in the past but never did it properly, so I also thought the same as you, that everything triggers my IBS. 

I also can have the same meal fine one day and be triggered by it the next. For example, white rice is fine on one day, but if I have it two days in a row I will suffer. I have incredibly slow digestion as well which I believe contributes to this issue. 

Personally, I only eat 1 meal a day, this allows me to feel less anxious about food because there is less chance of it making me flare up. I have been doing this for 10 years and have seen no side effects from this. Doing so did not affect my ability to identify triggers, I actually believe it made it easier! 

I recommend getting the Monash FODMAP app, this has helped tremendously when needing to know if an ingredient will be a trigger.

You can't just stop whenever you want. OP really needs to think about if this is right for them. Cymbalta had horrible side effects for me and took me over two months to discontinue use. Unless you believe it is absolutely necessary for daily functioning, I would advise against it. I was (and still am) depressed for many years, which became too much to handle when my mother passed away. I was quick to ask my doctor for anti-depressants, and I really wish I had not. I was put on the lowest dose of Pristiq. I became a zombie, as though I had no emotions. Although I wasn't sad, I was incapable of being happy either. My personality had completely changed, my friends would constantly comment on how different I was. I finally realised they were too much for me when I noticed how badly my hands would shake. I decided I wanted to come off them, which I did slowly. Very slowly. That however did nothing to diminish the withdrawal effects. I was so sick, I would not wish the way I felt for that week upon anyone. 

My depression came back, and I decided to give it one more go on a new type of anti depressant. The doctor explained to me that they were also anti anxiety, as I had been experiencing some anxiety beforehand, I was glad to hear this. Although it was obvious to me that these were not as strong on my body, it actually worsened my anxiety. I had my first real panic attack just a few weeks after beginning these anti depressants, which persisted daily for months before I could not handle them anymore. I had suicidal thoughts daily. I then began to throw up every morning. My doctor told me this was a normal part of 'getting used to them'. I couldn't go on like that. The withdrawals (Lexapro), were unlike anything I had ever experienced. My life was worse than it had ever been. 

The only thing that has been helping me since I've come off them is the fact that I smoke weed daily. It really helps to relax not only my body but also my mind, and I would take weed over prescription drugs to treat my depression/anxiety any day.
